subject: [PATCH v4 08/13] mm/collapse: call collapse_file() from collapse_single_pmd()

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed Zi Yan's concern about the writeback retry path, explaining that it only occurs after a dirty page has triggered a first collapse_file() call and a subsequent writeback, making the saving from one less page cache walk small and not measured. The author also mentioned that the scan rate change is in a separate patch where refused file tables no longer cause khugepaged to relock.
reviews.raw_body:
On the writeback retry, yes: one page cache walk less per retry.

But that path is MADV_COLLAPSE only, after a dirty page sent the first
collapse_file() back and the writeback has run, so it is rare and the
saving is small. Not measured.

The scan rate change is in the next patch, where a refused file table
no longer costs khugepaged a relock.

Not measured on the file side either, but it is the same shape as the
anonymous scan, where the relock per refused table was most of the cost
of a pass over memory that is already huge.

-- 
  Kiryl Shutsemau / Kirill A. Shutemov

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that moving collapse_file() call up into collapse_single_pmd() allows for a retry around the scan or the collapse alone, confirming the patch's approach.
reviews.raw_body:
Yep.

Once collapse_file() is called from here the retry can go around the
collapse alone or around the scan as well.

-- 
  Kiryl Shutsemau / Kirill A. Shutemov

2026-10-02.patch_summary: This patch moves the call to collapse_file() from collapse_scan_file() to collapse_single_pmd(). This change allows for a separate scan under mmap_lock and a run without it, and also enables mm_khugepaged_collapse_file to report on the status of collapsed tables. The writeback retry now re-runs collapse_file() alone instead of rescanning first, and mm_khugepaged_scan_file fires before the collapse, allowing its status to be read as SCAN_SUCCEED for accepted tables.
